nodes.n: A five-star ballroom. Chandeliers, cameras, the whole team in borrowed suits. The host announces: "Emerging Player of the Series."
And to present it: "Mr. Raghav Mehra."

nodes.t: A boy from a chai stall. Look at him now. I always say: this game rewards those who understand how it works.

nodes.n: He hands you the trophy. He doesn't let go of it. He leans in, smiling for the cameras.

nodes.t: You ran at ball three. I'll remember that. Rajgarh will remember it too.

choice.t: Take the microphone. Say it all. Live.
choice.d: In front of every camera in the country.

choice.t: Smile. Take the trophy. Let Rathore finish it quietly.

nodes.n: You turn to the microphone. The room goes silent the way a stadium goes silent before a big appeal.
You say everything. Jassi, Karan, the fire, ball three. Mehra laughs. "A talented boy with a vivid imagination. My lawyers will be in touch."
Without the proof in your hands, it's your word against a billionaire's. The cameras cut away.
You say everything. Then Rathore stands up at table nine and plays it through the ballroom speakers. His voice. His instructions. Ball three.

nodes.t: Turn that off. TURN IT OFF.

nodes.n: Four officers in plain clothes walk across the ballroom. The cameras don't cut away. Not one.
You smile. You take the trophy. At 2 AM, Rathore calls.

msgs.t: Not enough. His lawyers will eat it.
We'll keep watching. So will he.
Arrested at the airport. 1:40 AM. Trying to board his own jet.
No cameras. Your way was quieter. It worked.

nodes.t: Our boy. So sensible. I knew you would understand how the game works.

nodes.n: Rathore stands behind you, not unkindly, and puts a hand on your shoulder.

nodes.t: We'll talk after the dinner, {first}. Bring your phone.

nodes.cliff: Raghav Mehra walks out of the ballroom smiling. "See you next season, champ."
In handcuffs, Raghav Mehra laughs. "You think I'm the top of this? I'm a branch manager."
